    - heading "WITHOUT REPLACEMENT vs WITH REPLACEMENT" [level=2]
    - article:
      - heading "Without Replacement" [level=3]
      - text: 3 5 × 2 4 =
      - strong: 3/10 = 0.30
      - paragraph: After drawing a red, one red is removed.
      - button "Use without replacement"
    - article:
      - heading "With Replacement" [level=3]
      - text: 3 5 × 3 5 =
      - strong: 9/25 = 0.36
      - paragraph: The first red is put back, so counts reset.
      - button "Use with replacement"
    - article:
      - heading "Key Difference" [level=3]
      - paragraph: When a ball is not replaced, the sample space changes.
      - paragraph: Probabilities for the second draw depend on the first outcome.
    - article:
      - heading "THE RULE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B | A)
      - paragraph: Probability of A and then B equals probability of A times probability of B given A.
      - heading "Symmetric form" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(A ∩ B) = P(B) · P(A | B)
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Draw two without replacement. Find P(R then R).
      - list:
        - listitem: P(R₁) = 3/5
        - listitem: P(R₂ | R₁) = 2/4
        - listitem: P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = 3/5 × 2/4 = 6/20 = 3/10 = 0.30
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISTAKE" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISTAKE
      - paragraph: Do not use P(A) · P(B) unless A and B are independent.
      - paragraph: Here, R₁ and R₂ are dependent without replacement.
      - paragraph: "Wrong: 3/5 × 3/5 = 9/25 = 0.36 (too large)"
      - paragraph: "Correct: 3/5 × 2/4 = 3/10 = 0.30"
    - article:
      - heading "CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING
      - group "Which statement is always valid when P(R₁) > 0?":
        - text: Which statement is always valid when P(R₁) > 0?
        - radio "P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₁) · P(R₂)"
        - text: P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₁) · P(R₂)
        - radio "P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₁) · P(R₂ | R₁)"
        - text: P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₁) · P(R₂ | R₁)
        - radio "P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₂) · P(R₁)"
        - text: P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₂) · P(R₁)
        - radio "P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₁) + P(R₂)"
        - text: P(R₁ ∩ R₂) = P(R₁) + P(R₂)
      - button "Show explanation":
        - text: Show explanation
        - img
